what_it_is.prose: Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL) is a Navratna Category-I Public Sector Undertaking under the Ministry of Defence, Government of India, headquartered in Bengaluru. Founded in 1954, BEL is India's largest defence electronics OEM and the prime productioniser for many DRDO-developed systems. The company manufactures radars (Akash, Atulya, Weapon Locating Radar Swathi, BEL Shikari, Rohini, Revathi), electronic warfare systems (Sangraha, Samyukta), C4I systems (Akashteer Air Defence Control & Reporting System), simulators and training systems, fuzes, batteries, and laser-based Directed Energy Weapons. BEL's flagship counter-UAS product is the Integrated Drone Detection & Interdiction System (IDDIS) — Atlas slug cus-001 — produced under Transfer of Technology from DRDO's CHESS, LASTEC and LRDE laboratories. IDDIS entered operational service with the Indian Army in March 2024 and was deployed during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, where it conducted the first reported laser-DEW combat intercept of a hostile drone. On 16 May 2025, BEL signed a ₹572 crore contract with the Indian Army's Corps of Army Air Defence for additional IDDIS systems. For FY26, BEL reported revenue from operations of ₹27,479.6 crore (a 16.1% year-on-year increase from ₹23,658 crore in FY25), Profit After Tax of ₹6,048.5 crore (up 14.4% YoY), and a closing order book of ₹73,882 crore (including an export order book of USD 495 million). BEL's export sales for FY26 reached USD 141.9 million.

deployments_procurement.summary: BEL's FY26 was marked by record financial performance and several major contract wins. The Akashteer Air Defence Control & Reporting System, which BEL produces, was battle-proven during Operation Sindoor in May 2025 — the same operation in which BEL's IDDIS counter-drone system was deployed. The ₹572 crore IDDIS follow-on contract was signed on 16 May 2025. BEL's order book at the end of FY26 stood at ₹73,882 crore, the highest in the company's history, with FY26 fresh orders of approximately ₹30,000 crore (including export orders worth USD 346 million). BEL's export order book reached USD 495 million.

import_dependencies.summary: BEL is a Navratna PSU with stated vision of 'Atmanirbhar Bharat' and deep local content on radars, EW systems, C4I, simulators, fuzes, and batteries. However, the critical-component layer relies on global supply chains: FPGA (Xilinx/AMD, Intel/Altera — USA), GaN RF power amplifiers (Qorvo, Wolfspeed, MACOM — USA), EO/IR focal-plane arrays (Teledyne FLIR, SCD — USA / Israel), high-energy laser sources for DEW variants (IPG / Trumpf — Germany / USA), and IMU / fibre-optic gyros (Honeywell, Safran, Northrop — USA / France). BEL does not itemise these vendors in its annual report; only an aggregate 'indigenisation percentage' is reported.

faq.question: What is BEL's order book and FY26 financial performance?
faq.answer: BEL's order book stood at ₹73,882 crore as of 1 April 2026 (consolidated, including an export order book of USD 495 million) — the highest in the company's history. For FY26, BEL reported revenue from operations of ₹27,479.6 crore (up 16.1% YoY from ₹23,658 crore in FY25), Profit After Tax of ₹6,048.5 crore (up 14.4% YoY), and PBT of ₹8,075 crore (up 13.9% YoY). Fresh orders booked in FY26 were approximately ₹30,000 crore, including export orders worth USD 346 million. Export sales for FY26 were USD 141.9 million.

faq.question: What is BEL's role in Indian counter-UAS?
faq.answer: BEL is the prime productioniser of DRDO's Integrated Drone Detection & Interdiction System (IDDIS) — the Atlas slug cus-001 entry. IDDIS Mk-I entered operational service with the Indian Army in March 2024, conducted the first reported laser-DEW combat intercept on 13 April 2025, and was deployed during Operation Sindoor in May 2025. BEL signed a ₹572 crore follow-on contract on 16 May 2025. The IDDIS family includes Mk-I (2 kW laser, ~1 km hard-kill range), Mk-II (10 kW, 2 km range, cleared for induction December 2025), and Mk-IIA 'Sahastra Shakti' (30 kW, 5 km range).

faq.question: What is BEL's role in the BrahMos programme?
faq.answer: BEL produces seeker components and integration electronics for the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile programme (BrahMos Aerospace is a JV between DRDO 50.5% and Russia's NPOM 49.5%). BEL also produces the Akash SAM radar and C4I components, and is the productioniser for the IDDIS counter-drone system. BEL's FY26 export order book of USD 495 million includes BrahMos-related components and other defence electronics.
